text:
Marcus Pettersson is the Rangers' new stay-at-home defenseman, in his first season in New York after Pittsburgh and Vancouver. He plays 21 minutes a night, blocks shots (34) and almost never shoots, with four assists and no goals in 21 games. That's the job description.

This season's numbers are the uncomfortable part. The Rangers take 49% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, about 6 points worse than without him, and only 45% of the shot attempts. On a team that's been winning the chance battle almost every night lately, his pairing is one of the places where it leaks.

Last season told a different story. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 98th percentile for taking chances away after adjusting for teammates and competition, while noting he played with some of the weakest teammates in the league, which dragged down his raw numbers. Offense was never part of it: bottom 5% for creating. If that defensive impact is still there, this year's numbers should improve as the sample grows. Our talent range has him around 19 points. Watch the pairings once Sean Durzi is back.
